label: prop:aap
title: \protect\propositionname
body_md:
\label{prop:aap}Let $Q\subset N\subset M$ be inclusions of tracial
von Neumann algebras, with $M$ having separable predual. The following
conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every finite subset $F\subset N$, every $z\in M$, and every
$\eta,\epsilon>0$, there are a trace-preserving automorphism $\alpha$
of $M$ fixing $Q$ pointwise and $y\in N$ such that 
\[
\max_{a\in F}\|\alpha(a)-a\|_{2}<\eta,\qquad\|z-\alpha(y)\|_{2}<\epsilon.
\]
\item For every finite subset $F\subset N$ and every $\epsilon>0$, there
is a surjective trace-preserving isomorphism $\Phi:N\to M$ fixing
$Q$ pointwise such that 
\[
\max_{a\in F}\|\Phi(a)-a\|_{2}<\epsilon.
\]
\item There is a normal trace-preserving endomorphism $\rho:M\to M$ with
$\rho(M)=N$ which is a pointwise $L^{2}$ limit of a sequence of
trace-preserving automorphisms of $M$ fixing $Q$ pointwise.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, fix a unital von Neumann subalgebra $E\subset N$. Conditions
(1) and (2) remain equivalent if, for every additional tolerance $\kappa>0$,
the map $\alpha$, respectively $\Phi$, is required to satisfy
\[
\alpha(e)=UeU^{*},\quad\text{respectively }\Phi(e)=UeU^{*}\quad(e\in E),\qquad\|U-1\|<\kappa,
\]
for some unitary $U\in M$. The bound on $U-1$ is in operator norm.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $G=\operatorname{Aut}_{\tau,Q}(M)$ for the group of trace-preserving
automorphisms fixing $Q$ pointwise. We prove (1)$\Rightarrow$(2),
including the additional assertion about $E$; taking $E=\mathbb{C}1$
gives the original assertion. We use the Baire category argument of
\cite[Proposition 1]{ShlyakhtenkoFuchsian}, retaining both the restriction
of an automorphism and its implementing unitary.

Choose $L^{2}$-dense sequences $(a_{j})_{j\geq1}$ in $N$ and $(z_{j})_{j\geq1}$
in $M$. On the space of normal trace-preserving embeddings $N\to M$
fixing $Q$ pointwise, put 
\[
d(\phi,\psi)=\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}2^{-j}\min\{1,\|\phi(a_{j})-\psi(a_{j})\|_{2}\}.
\]
This metric induces pointwise $L^{2}$ convergence. The space is complete.
Indeed, if $(\phi_{n})$ is Cauchy, then for each $a\in N$ the sequence
$(\phi_{n}(a))$ is $L^{2}$-Cauchy and satisfies $\|\phi_{n}(a)\|=\|a\|$.
A uniformly operator-norm bounded $L^{2}$-Cauchy sequence has its
limit in $M$. These limits define a unital linear map on $N$, preserve
products and adjoints by continuity on norm-bounded sets, and preserve
the trace. Faithfulness of the trace makes it injective. It is normal:
if $b_{i}\uparrow b$ in $N_{+}$ and $c=\sup_{i}\phi(b_{i})$, then
$c\leq\phi(b)$ and normality of the traces gives $\tau(c)=\tau(b)=\tau(\phi(b))$,
hence $c=\phi(b)$. The condition of fixing $Q$ is closed.

Let $\mathcal{X}$ be the closure of
\[
\{(\alpha|_{N},U):\alpha\in G,\ U\in\mathcal{U}(M),\ \alpha|_{E}=\operatorname{Ad}U|_{E}\}
\]
in the product of this embedding space and the unitary group with
its operator-norm metric. This is a complete metric space containing
$(\iota,1)$, where $\iota:N\hookrightarrow M$ is inclusion. Every
$(\phi,U)\in\mathcal{X}$ still satisfies $\phi|_{E}=\operatorname{Ad}U|_{E}$.
For $j,k\geq1$, set
\[
\mathcal{O}_{j,k}=\{(\phi,U)\in\mathcal{X}:\text{ there is }y\in N\text{ with }\|z_{j}-\phi(y)\|_{2}<1/k\}.
\]
Each $\mathcal{O}_{j,k}$ is open, being a union of open conditions
on the value at a fixed $y$.

To see density, it suffices to approximate a pair $(\alpha_{0}|_{N},U_{0})$
from the set whose closure defines $\mathcal{X}$. A neighborhood
controls the first coordinate on a finite set $F\subset N$ and the
second coordinate in norm. Apply the strengthened condition (1) to
$F$ and $\alpha_{0}^{-1}(z_{j})$, obtaining $\beta\in G$, $y\in N$,
and an implementing unitary $V$ with both the displacement on $F$
and $\|V-1\|$ arbitrarily small, and with approximation error less
than $1/k$. Then $\alpha_{0}\beta$ is implemented on $E$ by $\alpha_{0}(V)U_{0}$,
and
\[
\begin{aligned}\|\alpha_{0}\beta(a)-\alpha_{0}(a)\|_{2} & =\|\beta(a)-a\|_{2}\quad(a\in F),\\
\|\alpha_{0}(V)U_{0}-U_{0}\| & =\|V-1\|,\\
\|z_{j}-\alpha_{0}\beta(y)\|_{2} & <1/k.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the resulting pair belongs to the given neighborhood and to $\mathcal{O}_{j,k}$.

By the Baire category theorem, $\bigcap_{j,k}\mathcal{O}_{j,k}$ is
dense in $\mathcal{X}$. If $(\phi,U)$ belongs to this intersection,
each $z_{j}$ belongs to the $L^{2}$ closure of $\phi(N)$. The image
$\phi(N)$ is a von Neumann subalgebra of $M$. Its trace-preserving
conditional expectation therefore fixes every $z_{j}$. By $L^{2}$
density, this expectation is the identity, so $\phi(N)=M$. Choosing
$(\phi,U)$ sufficiently close to $(\iota,1)$ on the prescribed finite
set and in the unitary coordinate proves (2), with the additional
bound on $\|U-1\|$.

For the original conditions, assume (2). By separability, choose surjective
trace-preserving isomorphisms $\Phi_{j}:N\to M$, fixing $Q$, which
converge pointwise in $L^{2}$ to the inclusion. Fix one surjective
trace-preserving isomorphism $\Phi:N\to M$ fixing $Q$. With $\iota:N\hookrightarrow M$
denoting inclusion, the maps 
\[
\gamma_{j}=\Phi_{j}\Phi^{-1}\in G
\]
converge pointwise in $L^{2}$ to $\rho=\iota\Phi^{-1}$, whose range
is $N$. This proves (3). Conversely, if $\gamma_{j}\to\rho$ as in
(3), then 
\[
\Phi_{j}=\gamma_{j}\rho^{-1}:N\to M
\]
are surjective trace-preserving isomorphisms fixing $Q$ and converging
to the inclusion. Thus (3)$\Rightarrow$(2).

It remains to prove (2)$\Rightarrow$(1), again including the additional
assertion. Given $F,z,\eta,\epsilon,\kappa$, choose a surjective
isomorphism $\Phi:N\to M$ fixing $Q$, moving each $a\in F$ by less
than $\eta/2$, and implemented on $E$ by a unitary $U$ with $\|U-1\|<\kappa/2$.
Put $y=\Phi^{-1}(z)\in N$. Choose a second surjective isomorphism
$\Psi:N\to M$ fixing $Q$, with
\[
\max_{a\in F}\|\Psi(a)-a\|_{2}<\eta/2,\qquad\|\Psi(y)-y\|_{2}<\epsilon,
\]
and implemented on $E$ by a unitary $V$ with $\|V-1\|<\kappa/2$.
The automorphism $\alpha=\Phi\Psi^{-1}$ belongs to $G$, and
\[
\|\alpha(a)-a\|_{2}\leq\|a-\Psi(a)\|_{2}+\|\Phi(a)-a\|_{2}<\eta\quad(a\in F),
\]
while
\[
\|\alpha(y)-z\|_{2}=\|\Psi^{-1}(y)-y\|_{2}=\|y-\Psi(y)\|_{2}<\epsilon.
\]
For $e\in E$, the identity $\alpha(VeV^{*})=UeU^{*}$ shows that
$\alpha|_{E}$ is implemented by $\alpha(V^{*})U$, and
\[
\|\alpha(V^{*})U-1\|\leq\|V-1\|+\|U-1\|<\kappa.
\]
This proves (1).

label: prop:caap
title: \protect\propositionname
body_md:
\label{prop:caap}Let $A\subset B\subset C$ be unital inclusions
of separable $C^{*}$-algebras, and let $\tau$ be a trace on $C$.
The following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every finite subset $F\subset B$, every $z\in C$, and every
$\eta,\epsilon>0$, there are a trace-preserving automorphism $\alpha$
of $C$ fixing $A$ pointwise and $y\in B$ such that 
\[
\max_{b\in F}\|\alpha(b)-b\|<\eta,\qquad\|z-\alpha(y)\|<\epsilon.
\]
\item For every finite subset $F\subset B$ and every $\epsilon>0$, there
is a surjective trace-preserving isomorphism $\Phi:B\to C$ fixing
$A$ pointwise such that 
\[
\max_{b\in F}\|\Phi(b)-b\|<\epsilon.
\]
\item There is a trace-preserving endomorphism $\rho:C\to C$ with $\rho(C)=B$
which is a point-norm limit of a sequence of trace-preserving automorphisms
of $C$ fixing $A$ pointwise.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, for a specified unital $C^{*}$-subalgebra $E\subset B$,
conditions (1) and (2) remain equivalent with the additional requirement
that, for every $\kappa>0$, the map be implemented on $E$ by a unitary
$U\in C$ with $\|U-1\|<\kappa$.

label: def:caap
title: \protect\definitionname
body_md:
\label{def:caap}An inclusion $B\subset C$ as in Proposition \ref{prop:caap}
has the $C^{*}$ Automorphism Approximation Property (CAAP) relative
to $A\subset B$ if the equivalent conditions of that proposition
hold. When $A=\mathbb{C}1$, we simply say that $B\subset C$ has
CAAP.
head: environment

label: def:inner-implementation
title: \protect\definitionname
body_md:
\label{def:inner-implementation}We say that AAP, respectively CAAP,
\textit{holds with small unitary implementation on a specified unital
subalgebra $E$} of the smaller algebra if the strengthened conditions
(1) and (2) in Proposition \ref{prop:aap}, respectively Proposition
\ref{prop:caap}, hold. The subalgebra $E$ is a von Neumann algebra
in the AAP case and a $C^{*}$-algebra in the CAAP case. Taking $E=\mathbb{C}1$
recovers the ordinary property.

label: rem:closures
title: \protect\remarkname
body_md:
\label{rem:closures}(1) Suppose that $A\subset B\subset C$ are separable
unital $C^{*}$-algebras, that $C$ carries a faithful tracial state
$\tau$, and that $B\subset C$ has CAAP relative to $A$, with trace-preserving
witnessing maps. Then, in the GNS representation of $\tau$, the inclusion
$W^{*}(B)\subset W^{*}(C)$ has AAP relative to $W^{*}(A)$. If CAAP
holds with small unitary implementation on $E\subset B$, then AAP
holds with small unitary implementation on $W^{*}(E)$: extend the
surjective trace-preserving isomorphisms to the generated von Neumann
algebras, retaining the same implementing unitaries.

(2) Having AAP or CAAP relative to a subalgebra implies the same property
relative to any smaller unital subalgebra.
head: environment

label: rem:implementation
title: \protect\remarkname
body_md:
\label{rem:implementation}If $N=W^{*}(Q,E)$, then fixing $Q$ and
conjugating $E$ by unitaries converging in norm to $1$ already imply
pointwise $L^{2}$ convergence to the inclusion. The corresponding
statement holds in norm when $B=C^{*}(A,E)$. Thus, in this situation,
the finite-set approximation condition follows from the requirement
of small unitary implementation.

For CAAP, small unitary implementation on $E$ is equivalent to small
unitary implementation on $TET^{*}$ for any $T\in\mathcal{U}(B)$,
with the fixed subalgebra $A$ unchanged. Indeed, if $\Phi|_{E}=\operatorname{Ad}U|_{E}$,
then $\Phi$ is implemented on $TET^{*}$ by $W=\Phi(T)UT^{*}$, and
\[
\|W-1\|\leq\|\Phi(T)-T\|+\|U-1\|.
\]
We can choose $F$ to contain $T$, thus bounding $\Vert\Phi(T)-T\Vert$.
Replacing $T$ by $T^{*}$ proves the converse.

label: ex:infinite-free-product
title: \protect\examplename
body_md:
\label{ex:infinite-free-product}Let $(P_{j},\tau_{j})$, $j\geq0$,
be trace-preserving copies of a tracial von Neumann algebra $(P,\tau)$
with separable predual. Put $N=*_{j\geq1}(P_{j},\tau_{j})$ and $M=(P_{0},\tau_{0})*N$.
Then $N\subset M$ has AAP, relative to any fixed initial free product
$Q=P_{1}*\cdots*P_{r}$.

Similarly, let $(\mathcal{B},\tau)$ be a separable unital $C^{*}$-algebra
with a faithful tracial state, and let $(B_{j},\tau_{j})$, $j\geq0$,
be trace-preserving copies of $(\mathcal{B},\tau)$. Then the reduced
free-product inclusion $B=*_{\mathrm{red},\,j\geq1}(B_{j},\tau_{j})\subset(B_{0},\tau_{0})*_{\mathrm{red}}B$
has CAAP relative to $A=*_{\mathrm{red},\,j=1}^{r}(B_{j},\tau_{j})$
for every $r\geq1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Given a finite $F\subset N$ and $z\in M$ and $\eta,\epsilon>0$,
choose $m\geq r$ so that every $a\in F$ has an approximation $a^{\prime}\in P_{1}*\cdots*P_{m}$
with $\|a-a^{\prime}\|_{2}<\eta/2$, and choose $z^{\prime}\in P_{0}*P_{1}*\cdots*P_{m}$
with $\|z-z^{\prime}\|_{2}<\epsilon$. Choose $j>m$. Consider the
automorphism $\alpha:M\to M$ that switches $P_{0}$ and $P_{j}$,
and fixes all other components. Then $\alpha$ fixes $P_{1}*\cdots*P_{m}\supset Q$
pointwise. Moreover 
\[
P_{0}*P_{1}*\cdots*P_{m}\subset\alpha(N).
\]
Hence $y=\alpha^{-1}(z^{\prime})$ belongs to $N$, and 
\[
\|\alpha(a)-a\|_{2}\leq2\|a-a^{\prime}\|_{2}<\eta\quad(a\in F),\qquad\|z-\alpha(y)\|_{2}<\epsilon.
\]
This proves AAP relative to $Q$. The proof of the $C^{*}$-algebra
version is identical.

label: ex:abelian-coordinate
title: \protect\examplename
body_md:
(a) Let $R=\overline{\bigotimes}M_{2\times2}$ be the hyperfinite
II$_{1}$ factor. Then $R\otimes1\subset R\otimes R$ has AAP.

\label{ex:abelian-coordinate}(b) Let $X=\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ be
the Cantor set with the product measure $\prod(\frac{1}{2}\delta_{0}+\frac{1}{2}\delta_{1})$.
Then the inclusion 
\[
C(X)\otimes1\subset C(X\times X)
\]
has trace-preserving CAAP.

(c) The coordinate inclusion 
\[
N=L^{\infty}([0,1])\otimes1\subset M=L^{\infty}([0,1]^{2}),
\]
with Lebesgue probability measure, has AAP.

label: exa:MainExamples
title: \protect\examplename
body_md:
\label{exa:MainExamples}(a) Let $n\geq2$, $B=C_{\mathrm{red}}^{*}(\mathbb{F}_{n})$
and $C=B*_{\mathrm{red}}C^{*}(S)$, where $S$ is a free semicircular
element. The inclusion $B\subset C$ has CAAP with trace-preserving
witnessing maps. In particular, $B\cong C$. This example is the direct
application of Theorem \ref{thm:free-absorption} proved in this paper.

(b) Let $n\geq2$, $N=L(\mathbb{F}_{n})$ and $M=N*L(\mathbb{Z})\cong L(\mathbb{F}_{n+1})$.
The inclusion $N\subset M$ has AAP, and hence $N\cong M$. This follows
from (a) and Remark \ref{rem:closures}(1), since the von Neumann
algebra generated by a semicircular element is diffuse abelian. 

(c) Let $M=L(\mathbb{F}_{2})$ be generated by free Haar unitaries
$a,b$. Put $w=aba^{-1}b^{-1}$, $N=W^{*}(a,w)$ and $Q=W^{*}(w)$.
The construction in \cite{ShlyakhtenkoFuchsian} gives AAP for $N\subset M$
relative to $Q$. Since $a$ and $w$ are free Haar unitaries, a surjective
isomorphism $\Phi:N\to M$ fixing $Q$ gives 
\[
M=\Phi(W^{*}(w)*W^{*}(a))=W^{*}(w)*W^{*}(v),\qquad v=\Phi(a).
\]
Thus $Q$ is freely complemented in $M$.

label: prop:permanence
title: \protect\propositionname
body_md:
\label{prop:permanence}The following statements hold for AAP in tracial
von Neumann algebras with separable predual, and for CAAP in separable
unital $C^{*}$-algebras with a fixed trace.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $Q\subset L\subset N\subset M$ and both $L\subset N$ and $N\subset M$
have the property relative to $Q$, then $L\subset M$ has the property
relative to $Q$.
\item Let $Q\subset N_{0}\subset N_{1}\subset\cdots$ be an increasing sequence,
with each $N_{n}\subset N_{n+1}$ having the property relative to
$Q$. Put 
\[
M=\overline{\bigcup_{n\geq0}N_{n}}^{\|\cdot\|}\quad\text{in the }C^{*}\text{ case},\qquad M=\overline{\bigcup_{n\geq0}N_{n}}^{WOT}\quad\text{in the tracial case}.
\]
Then every $N_{n}\subset M$ has the same property relative to $Q$.
\end{enumerate}
Both assertions remain valid with small unitary implementation on
a common unital subalgebra $E$ contained in the smallest algebra.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the characterization by surjective isomorphisms in Propositions
\ref{prop:aap}(2) and \ref{prop:caap}(2), including its strengthened
version. Write $d(x,y)=\|x-y\|$ in the $C^{*}$ case and $d(x,y)=\|x-y\|_{2}$
in the tracial case. Taking $E=\mathbb{C}1$ gives the ordinary assertions.

For (1), given a finite $F\subset L$ and $\epsilon,\kappa>0$, choose
a surjective isomorphism $\phi:L\to N$ moving $F$ by less than $\epsilon/2$,
implemented on $E$ by $U$ with $\|U-1\|<\kappa/2$. Choose a surjective
isomorphism $\psi:N\to M$ moving $\phi(F)$ by less than $\epsilon/2$,
implemented on $E$ by $V$ with $\|V-1\|<\kappa/2$. Both maps fix
$Q$. Their composition has the required finite-set approximation
and is implemented on $E$ by $\psi(U)V$, with
\[
\|\psi(U)V-1\|\leq\|U-1\|+\|V-1\|<\kappa.
\]

For (2), it suffices to treat $N_{0}\subset M$. Fix a finite $F\subset N_{0}$
and $\epsilon,\kappa>0$, and choose positive numbers $\epsilon_{n},\kappa_{n}$
with $\sum_{n\geq0}\epsilon_{n}<\epsilon$ and $\sum_{n\geq0}\kappa_{n}<\kappa$.
Choose increasing finite sets $H_{n}\subset N_{n}$ whose union is
$d$-dense in $M$, and a $d$-dense sequence $(a_{j})$ in $N_{0}$.
Starting with $\phi_{0}=\mathrm{id}_{N_{0}}$ and $U_{0}=1$, construct
surjective isomorphisms $\phi_{n}:N_{0}\to N_{n}$ fixing $Q$ and
satisfying $\phi_{n}|_{E}=\operatorname{Ad}U_{n}|_{E}$. At stage
$n$, choose a finite set $F_{n}\subset N_{0}$ containing $F$, all
previous $F_{j}$, the first $n$ elements $a_{j}$, and $\phi_{n}^{-1}(H_{n})$.
Choose a surjective isomorphism $\psi_{n}:N_{n}\to N_{n+1}$ fixing
$Q$, moving every element of $\phi_{n}(F_{n})\cup\{U_{n}\}$ by less
than $\epsilon_{n}$, and implemented on $E$ by $V_{n}$ with $\|V_{n}-1\|<\kappa_{n}$.
Set
\[
\phi_{n+1}=\psi_{n}\phi_{n},\qquad U_{n+1}=\psi_{n}(U_{n})V_{n}.
\]
Then $\phi_{n+1}|_{E}=\operatorname{Ad}U_{n+1}|_{E}$, and
\[
\begin{aligned}d(\phi_{n+1}(a),\phi_{n}(a)) & <\epsilon_{n}\quad(a\in F_{n}),\\
d(U_{n+1},U_{n}) & <\epsilon_{n}+\kappa_{n},\\
\|U_{n+1}-1\| & \leq\|U_{n}-1\|+\kappa_{n}.
\end{aligned}
\]

The maps $\phi_{n}$ converge pointwise for $d$ to an embedding $\phi:N_{0}\to M$,
fixing $Q$ and moving $F$ by less than $\epsilon$. In the tracial
case, the uniform bounds $\|\phi_{n}(a)\|=\|a\|$ ensure that the
limits lie in $M$ and preserve multiplication; trace preservation
gives normality, as in Proposition \ref{prop:aap}. The unitaries
$U_{n}$ converge for $d$ to a unitary $U$. In the tracial case
this follows because both $U_{n}$ and $U_{n}^{*}$ are $L^{2}$-Cauchy
and uniformly bounded. The uniform operator-norm bound passes to the
limit, giving
\[
\phi|_{E}=\operatorname{Ad}U|_{E},\qquad\|U-1\|\leq\sum_{n\geq0}\kappa_{n}<\kappa.
\]

To see surjectivity, fix $b\in\bigcup_{n}H_{n}$. For every sufficiently
large $n$, put $a_{n,b}=\phi_{n}^{-1}(b)\in F_{n}$. Retaining this
element in all subsequent control sets gives
\[
d(\phi(a_{n,b}),b)\leq\sum_{j\geq n}\epsilon_{j}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the range is $d$-dense. In the $C^{*}$ case it is norm closed.
In the tracial case its trace-preserving conditional expectation fixes
a $d$-dense set and hence is the identity. Therefore $\phi$ is surjective.
All maps preserve the specified trace.

label: lem:flow
title: \protect\lemmaname
body_md:
\label{lem:flow}Suppose that $B_{0}=\mathop{{*}\text{-}\mathrm{Alg}}\nolimits(A,X)$,
where $A\subset B_{0}$ is a unital $*$-subalgebra and $X\in B_{0}$.
Suppose that $\delta$ is real, $\delta|_{A}=0$, and $\xi=\delta^{*}(1\otimes1)\in B_{0}$.
Then the formulas 
\[
D(b)=\delta(b)\#S\quad(b\in B_{0}),\qquad D(S)=-\xi
\]
define a $*$-derivation $D:C_{0}\to C_{0}$ satisfying $\tau(Dp)=0$
for every $p\in C_{0}$. It generates a global point-norm continuous
one-parameter group $(\alpha_{t})_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ of trace-preserving
automorphisms of $C$, fixing $A$ pointwise, with 
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\alpha_{t}(p)=\alpha_{t}(Dp),\qquad p\in C_{0}.
\]
In particular, 
\[
\|\alpha_{t}(X)-X\|\leq|t|\,\|\delta(X)\#S\|.
\]

If the restriction of $\delta$ to a unital $*$-subalgebra $E\subset B_{0}$
is inner, say 
\[
\delta(b)=Qb-bQ\quad(b\in E),\qquad Q\in B_{0}\otimes B_{0}^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad Q^{\dagger}=-Q,
\]
then there are norm continuously differentiable unitaries $U_{t}\in C$,
with $U_{0}=1$, such that 
\[
\alpha_{t}(b)=U_{t}bU_{t}^{*}\quad(b\in C^{*}(E)),\qquad\|U_{t}-1\|\leq|t|\,\|Q\#S\|.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The construction in \cite[Appendix, Proposition 21]{ShlyakhtenkoMicrostates}
gives the derivation $D$ and the identity $\tau(Dp)=0$. Only finitely
many coefficients from $A$ occur in the polynomial expressions for
$D(X)$ and $D(S)$; note that $D$ annihilates $A$. The analytic-vector
argument in \cite[Theorem 2.7 and Corollary 3.7]{VoiculescuCyclomorphy}
therefore yields a one-parameter group $(\alpha_{t})$ of trace-preserving
automorphisms of $W^{*}(C)$. For sufficiently small $|t|$, the power
series for $\alpha_{t}(X)$ and $\alpha_{t}(S)$ converge in operator
norm to elements of $C$. Since $\alpha_{t}$ fixes $A$, this gives
$\alpha_{t}(C)\subset C$. Applying the same argument to $-t$ gives
equality for sufficiently small $|t|$. For arbitrary $t\in\mathbb{R}$,
choose $n$ so large that this applies to $t/n$; then $\alpha_{t}=(\alpha_{t/n})^{n}$
gives $\alpha_{t}(C)=C$. The maps $t\mapsto\alpha_{t}(y)$ are norm
continuous for every $y\in C$ and norm differentiable for $y\in C_{0}$.

For the operator-norm estimate needed here, norm differentiability
gives 
\[
\alpha_{t}(y)-y=\int_{0}^{t}\alpha_{s}(D(y))\,ds\qquad\forall y\in C_{0},
\]
with the integral taken in operator norm. Since each $\alpha_{s}$
is isometric, 
\[
\|\alpha_{t}(y)-y\|\leq|t|\,\|D(y)\|.
\]
Taking $y=X$ gives the first estimate.

For the restriction to $E$, put $H=Q\#S$. Then $H^{*}=-H$ and $D(b)=[H,b]$
for $b\in E$. Consider 
\[
\frac{d}{dt}U_{t}=\alpha_{t}(H)U_{t},\qquad U_{0}=1.
\]
This bounded linear differential equation has a global unitary solution.
Both $\alpha_{t}(b)$ and $U_{t}bU_{t}^{*}$ solve $\frac{d}{dt}Y_{t}=[\alpha_{t}(H),Y_{t}]$
with initial value $b$, so uniqueness gives the claimed equality,
first on $E$ and then on $C^{*}(E)$. Finally, integration gives
\[
\|U_{t}-1\|\leq|t|\,\|H\|.
\]

label: lem:gaussian-bound
title: \protect\lemmaname
body_md:
\label{lem:gaussian-bound}Let $S$ be standard semicircular and free
from a faithfully tracial $C^{*}$-algebra $B$. For a finite tensor
$U\in B\otimes B^{\mathrm{op}}$, 
\[
\frac{1}{2}\|U\|_{\mathrm{rc}}\leq\|U\#S\|\leq\|U\|_{\mathrm{rc}}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $U=\sum_{i}a_{i}\otimes b_{i}^{\mathrm{op}}$. Use the Fock
realization over the coarse bimodule of $M=W^{*}(B)$ described in
Connes-{}-Shlyakhtenko \cite[Appendix II]{ConnesShlyakhtenko}. In
this realization, $S=\ell+\ell^{*}$ and $\ell^{*}b\ell=\tau(b)1$
for $b\in M$; see \cite[equation (6.1)]{ConnesShlyakhtenko}. For
$L=\sum_{i}a_{i}\ell b_{i}$, one has 
\[
L^{*}L=\sum_{i,j}b_{i}^{*}\tau(a_{i}^{*}a_{j})b_{j},
\]
so that $\|L\|=\bigl\|\sum_{i,j}b_{i}^{*}\tau(a_{i}^{*}a_{j})b_{j}\bigr\|^{1/2}$.
Applying the same calculation to the adjoint of $\sum_{i}a_{i}\ell^{*}b_{i}$
and using the triangle inequality proves the upper bound.

For the lower bound, put $Y=U\#S$ and let $E_{M}$ be the trace-preserving
conditional expectation onto $M$. Freeness gives 
\[
E_{M}(Y^{*}Y)=\sum_{i,j}b_{i}^{*}\tau(a_{i}^{*}a_{j})b_{j},\qquad E_{M}(YY^{*})=\sum_{i,j}a_{i}\tau(b_{i}b_{j}^{*})a_{j}^{*}.
\]
Since $E_{M}$ is contractive, each term in $\|U\|_{\mathrm{rc}}$
is at most $\|Y\|$.

label: prop:absorption
title: \protect\propositionname
body_md:
\label{prop:absorption}Let $(B,\tau)$ be separable, unital and faithfully
tracial. Let $B_{0}\subset B$ be a dense unital $*$-subalgebra algebraically
generated by a unital $*$-subalgebra $A$ and an element $X$. Let
$S$ and $C$ be as above. Assume that for every $\epsilon,\eta>0$
there is a real derivation $\delta:B_{0}\to B_{0}\otimes B_{0}^{\mathrm{op}}$
such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\delta|_{A}=0$;
\item The conjugate variable $\xi=\delta^{*}(1\otimes1)$ exists and belongs
to $B_{0}$;
\item $\|\delta(X)\|_{\mathrm{rc}}<\eta$;
\item $\|\delta(\xi)-1\otimes1\|_{\mathrm{rc}}<\epsilon$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $B\subset C$ has CAAP relative to $C^{*}(A)$. Thus $N=W^{*}(B)\subset W^{*}(C)=M$
has AAP relative to $Q=W^{*}(A)$.

Moreover, suppose that one of these derivations is inner on a unital
$*$-subalgebra $E\subset B_{0}$, with $\delta(b)=\Theta b-b\Theta$
for $b\in E$, where $\Theta\in B_{0}\otimes B_{0}^{\mathrm{op}}$
and $\Theta^{\dagger}=-\Theta$. Then the local approximating automorphism
$\alpha=\alpha_{\pi/2}$ constructed in the proof satisfies
\[
\alpha(b)=UbU^{*}\quad(b\in C^{*}(E)),\qquad\|U-1\|\leq\frac{\pi}{2}\|\Theta\#S\|\leq\frac{\pi}{2}\|\Theta\|_{\mathrm{rc}}
\]
for a unitary $U\in C$. Consequently, if for every $\epsilon,\eta,\kappa>0$
the derivation can be chosen to satisfy (1)-{}-(4) and to be inner
on this fixed $E$ with $\|\Theta\|_{\mathrm{rc}}<\kappa$, then CAAP
holds with small unitary implementation on $C^{*}(E)$, and AAP holds
with small unitary implementation on $W^{*}(E)$.
head: environment

label: eq:xiMovedToS
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\delta,\xi$ satisfy the hypotheses, and let $(\alpha_{t})$
be the one-parameter group supplied by Lemma \ref{lem:flow}. Put
\[
e=D(\xi)-S=(\delta(\xi)-1\otimes1)\#S.
\]
By Lemma \ref{lem:gaussian-bound}, $\|e\|\leq\|\delta(\xi)-1\otimes1\|_{\mathrm{rc}}<\epsilon$,
and 
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\alpha_{t}(\xi)=\alpha_{t}(S)+\alpha_{t}(e),\qquad\frac{d}{dt}\alpha_{t}(S)=-\alpha_{t}(\xi).
\]
Thus
\[
\alpha_{t}(\xi)=(\cos t)\xi+(\sin t)S+\int_{0}^{t}\cos(t-s)\alpha_{s}(e)\,ds.
\]
Since every $\alpha_{s}$ is isometric, evaluating at $t=\pi/2$ gives
\begin{equation}
\|\alpha_{\pi/2}(\xi)-S\|\leq\|e\|<\epsilon.\label{eq:xiMovedToS}
\end{equation}
At the same time, $\|\delta(X)\#S\|\leq\|\delta(X)\|_{\mathrm{rc}}<\eta$,
so 
\[
\|\alpha_{\pi/2}(X)-X\|<\frac{\pi}{2}\eta,\qquad\alpha_{\pi/2}|_{C^{*}(A)}=\mathrm{id}.
\]

The estimate for inner restrictions follows from Lemma \ref{lem:flow},
with $U=U_{\pi/2}$, and Lemma \ref{lem:gaussian-bound}. Under the
additional hypothesis, we can impose $\|\Theta\|_{\mathrm{rc}}<2\kappa/\pi$
along with the choices of $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ below. The resulting
automorphism then has an implementing unitary within $\kappa$ of
$1$, so the same argument verifies the strengthened condition (1)
of Proposition \ref{prop:caap}.

We now verify condition (1) of Proposition \ref{prop:caap}. Let $F=\{z_{1},\dots,z_{k}\}\subset B$
be a finite set, $z\in C$, and $\eta^{\prime},\epsilon^{\prime}>0$.
Choose $*$-polynomials $p_{1},\dots,p_{k}$ with coefficients from
$A$ so that $\Vert p_{j}(X)-z_{j}\Vert<\eta'/3$, $j=1,\dots,k$,
and a $*$-polynomial in two noncommuting variables with coefficients
from $A$ so that $\Vert p(X,S)-z\Vert<\epsilon'/2$. These polynomial
functions are Lipschitz on norm-bounded sets. Taking $\epsilon<1$,
the preceding estimates give $\|\alpha_{\pi/2}(\xi)\|<3$ and $\|\alpha_{\pi/2}(X)\|=\|X\|$,
so the Lipschitz constants may be chosen independently of the derivation.
We can therefore choose $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ sufficiently small
so that, writing $\alpha=\alpha_{\pi/2}$,
\[
\Vert p_{j}(\alpha(X))-p_{j}(X)\Vert<\eta'/3,\qquad j=1,\dots,k
\]
and
\[
\Vert p(\alpha(X),\alpha(\xi))-p(X,S)\Vert<\epsilon'/2.
\]
Noting that $\alpha(p_{j}(X))=p_{j}(\alpha(X))$ gives us
\[
\begin{aligned}\|\alpha(z_{j})-z_{j}\| & \leq\|\alpha(z_{j})-\alpha(p_{j}(X))\|\\
 & \quad+\|p_{j}(\alpha(X))-p_{j}(X)\|+\|p_{j}(X)-z_{j}\|<\eta'.
\end{aligned}
\]
Likewise, noting that $\alpha(p(X,\xi))=p(\alpha(X),\alpha(\xi))$,
and setting $y=p(X,\xi)\in B$,
\[
\|z-\alpha(y)\|\leq\|z-p(X,S)\|+\|p(X,S)-p(\alpha(X),\alpha(\xi))\|<\epsilon'.
\]
Thus condition (1) is verified, and the proof of CAAP is finished.
Remark \ref{rem:closures}(1) now gives AAP for $N\subset M$ relative
to $Q$.
head: environment

label: rem:xiIsCloseToSemicircular
title: \protect\remarkname
body_md:
\label{rem:xiIsCloseToSemicircular}Equation \ref{eq:xiMovedToS},
with $\alpha=\alpha_{\pi/2}$, gives 
\[
\|\xi-\alpha^{-1}(S)\|=\|\alpha(\xi)-S\|<\epsilon.
\]
Since $\alpha$ preserves the trace, $\alpha^{-1}(S)$ is standard
semicircular. Thus $\xi$ is within $\epsilon$ in operator norm of
a semicircular element in the enlarged algebra $C$.

label: lem:sparse-clt
title: \protect\lemmaname
body_md:
\label{lem:sparse-clt}For each $m$, let $g_{m,1},\ldots,g_{m,N_{m}}$
belong to a discrete group $G_{m}$, with $N_{m}\to\infty$. Suppose
that for every fixed $p\geq1$, and all sufficiently large $m$, the
following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If a word of length at most $2p$ in the letters $g_{m,j}^{\pm1}$
equals the identity, then the total degree of each letter must be
zero.
\item All but $O(N_{m}^{p-1})$ of the $p$-element subsets of letters are
free inside $G_{m}$.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\lambda_{m}$ be the left regular representation of $G_{m}$.
Then for any signs $\varepsilon_{m,j}\in\{-1,1\}$, the sums 
\[
Z_{m}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{N_{m}}}\sum_{j=1}^{N_{m}}\varepsilon_{m,j}\lambda_{m}(g_{m,j})
\]
converge in $*$-distribution to a standard circular element.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let
\[
H_{m}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{N_{m}}}\sum_{j=1}^{N_{m}}\varepsilon_{m,j}u_{j},
\]
where the $u_{j}$ are freely independent Haar unitaries.

Let $q(x,x^{*})=x^{\epsilon(1)}x^{\epsilon(2)}\cdots x^{\epsilon(r)}$
be a $*$-monomial of degree $r$, where $\epsilon:\{1,\dots,r\}\to\{\cdot,*\}$.
Then
\begin{align}
\tau(q(Z_{m},Z_{m}^{*})) & =N_{m}^{-\frac{r}{2}}\sum_{j_{1},\dots,j_{r}=1}^{N_{m}}\varepsilon_{m,j_{1}}\cdots\varepsilon_{m,j_{r}}\tau(\lambda_{m}(g_{m,j_{1}})^{\epsilon(1)}\cdots\lambda_{m}(g_{m,j_{r}})^{\epsilon(r)})\label{eq:expansionZm}\\
\tau(q(H_{m},H_{m}^{*})) & =N_{m}^{-\frac{r}{2}}\sum_{j_{1},\dots,j_{r}=1}^{N_{m}}\varepsilon_{m,j_{1}}\cdots\varepsilon_{m,j_{r}}\tau(u_{j_{1}}^{\epsilon(1)}\cdots u_{j_{r}}^{\epsilon(r)}).\label{eq:expansionHm}
\end{align}
Because of (1), for large enough $m$, the term $\tau(\lambda_{m}(g_{m,j_{1}})^{\epsilon(1)}\cdots\lambda_{m}(g_{m,j_{r}})^{\epsilon(r)})$
vanishes unless the total degree of each letter $g_{m,k}$ is zero.
The same condition is necessary for $\tau(u_{j_{1}}^{\epsilon(1)}\cdots u_{j_{r}}^{\epsilon(r)})$
to be nonzero, by freeness. Thus, for nonzero terms, it is possible
to pair up the integers $\{1,\dots,r\}$ in such a way that if $k$
is paired with $k'$ then $j_{k}=j_{k'}$ and $\epsilon(k)\neq\epsilon(k')$.
Thus it must be that $r$ is even (so $r=2p$ for some $p$); moreover,
there cannot be more than $p$ distinct letters. Thus we only need
to keep terms in the summations (\ref{eq:expansionZm}) and (\ref{eq:expansionHm})
in which the indices $j_{1},\dots,j_{2p}$ take on at most $p$ distinct
values.

There are at most $O(N_{m}^{p-1})$ terms in which the indices $j_{1},\dots,j_{2p}$
take on at most $p-1$ distinct values.

By (2), among terms in (\ref{eq:expansionZm}) in which the indices
$j_{1},\dots,j_{2p}$ take on exactly $p$ distinct values, all but
$O(N_{m}^{p-1})$ involve letters that freely generate a free subgroup,
and therefore equal the corresponding term in (\ref{eq:expansionHm}).

It follows that the difference between (\ref{eq:expansionZm}) and
(\ref{eq:expansionHm}) involves a summation over at most $O(N_{m}^{p-1})$
terms, each of which has absolute value at most one. Noting the prefactor
$N_{m}^{-r/2}=N_{m}^{-p}$, we see that for large enough $m$,
\[
\tau(q(Z_{m},Z_{m}^{*}))=\tau(q(H_{m},H_{m}^{*}))+O(N_{m}^{-1}).
\]

The usual free central limit theorem (see e.g. \cite[Lectures 11--12]{NicaSpeicher})
then implies that the limit law of $(H_{m},H_{m}^{*})$ (and thus
of $(Z_{m},Z_{m}^{*})$) is the circular law.

label: lem:cocycle
title: \protect\lemmaname
body_md:
\label{lem:cocycle}Let $G=\mathbb{F}_{2}=\langle a,b\rangle$, and
let $\lambda$ be its left regular representation on $\ell^{2}(G)$.
For every $\eta>0$, there are a finitely supported real vector $x\in\ell^{2}(G)$,
and $w\in G\setminus\{e\}$ such that the cocycle $c:G\to\ell^{2}(G)$
determined by 
\[
c(a)=(1-\lambda(a))x,\qquad c(b)=0
\]
satisfies 
\[
\|x\|_{2}<\eta,\qquad\|c(w)-\delta_{e}\|_{2}<\eta.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $x\in\ell^{2}(G)$ be an arbitrary real coefficient vector to
be chosen later, and let $c$ be the cocycle determined by $c(a)=(1-\lambda(a))x$
and $c(b)=0$.

For $m\geq1$, put 
\[
M=m+2,\qquad r_{j}=M^{j}-M^{j-1},\qquad w_{m}=\prod_{j=1}^{m}a^{r_{j}}b^{r_{j}}.
\]
Write 
\[
g_{j}=\prod_{i<j}a^{r_{i}}b^{r_{i}},\qquad h_{j}=g_{j}a^{r_{j}},\qquad R_{m}=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\bigl(\lambda(g_{j})-\lambda(h_{j})\bigr).
\]
Since $c$ is inner on $\langle a\rangle$, $c(a^{r_{j}})=(1-\lambda(a^{r_{j}}))x$.
Since $c(b)=0$, the cocycle identity implies that $c(w_{m})=R_{m}x$.

Let $\tau$ be the canonical trace on $L(G)$. We apply Lemma \ref{lem:sparse-clt}
to the $2m-1$ group elements 
\[
g_{2},\ldots,g_{m},\ h_{1},\ldots,h_{m}.
\]
For condition (1), note that the total degree of $a$ or $b$ in $g_{j}$
is $\sum_{i<j}r_{i}=M^{j-1}-1$. The total degree of $a$ in $h_{j}$
is $M^{j}-1$, and the total degree of $b$ in $h_{j}$ is $M^{j-1}-1$.
Thus, if a word in the letters $g_{2},\dots,g_{m},h_{1},\dots,h_{m}$
of length at most $2p$ reduces to the identity, and the total degree
of $g_{k}$ is $t_{k}$ and the total degree of $h_{k}$ is $s_{k}$
(with $t_{1}=0$), then
\[
\sum t_{k}(M^{k-1}-1)+\sum s_{k}(M^{k-1}-1)=0
\]
(because the total degree of $b$ must be zero) and
\[
\sum t_{k}(M^{k-1}-1)+\sum s_{k}(M^{k}-1)=0
\]
(because the total degree of $a$ must be zero). Subtracting these
we get
\[
(M-1)\sum s_{k}M^{k-1}=0.
\]
Since each $|s_{k}|\leq2p$, this forces $s_{k}=0$ once $M$ is large
enough. It follows that also $\sum t_{k}(M^{k-1}-1)=0$, which, because
$|t_{k}|\leq2p$, also forces $t_{k}=0$ for large enough $M$.

For condition (2), choose
\[
\begin{gathered}3\leq j_{1}<\cdots<j_{p}\leq m,\qquad j_{i+1}-j_{i}\geq2\quad(1\leq i<p),\\
v_{i}\in\{g_{j_{i}},h_{j_{i}}\}\qquad(1\leq i\leq p).
\end{gathered}
\]
Only $O_{p}(m^{p-1})$ selections fail these conditions. Write
\[
\begin{gathered}s_{2j-1}=a^{r_{j}},\qquad s_{2j}=b^{r_{j}},\qquad n_{0}=0,\\
v_{i}=s_{1}\cdots s_{n_{i}},\qquad n_{i}\in\{2j_{i}-2,2j_{i}-1\}.
\end{gathered}
\]
With $v_{0}=e$, put
\[
d_{i}=v_{i-1}^{-1}v_{i}=s_{n_{i-1}+1}\cdots s_{n_{i}},\qquad\ell(d_{i})=n_{i}-n_{i-1}\geq3,
\]
where $\ell$ counts the nonzero powers in the reduced alternating
expression in $a,b$. Since $r_{j}\ne r_{k}$ for $j\ne k$, complete
cancellation of adjacent powers in a product of the $d_{i}^{\pm1}$
can occur only between $d_{i}$ and $d_{i}^{-1}$. Thus, for $\varepsilon_{\nu}\in\{-1,1\}$
with
\[
(i_{\nu+1},\varepsilon_{\nu+1})\ne(i_{\nu},-\varepsilon_{\nu})\qquad(1\leq\nu<k),
\]
we have
\[
\ell\!\left(d_{i_{1}}^{\varepsilon_{1}}\cdots d_{i_{k}}^{\varepsilon_{k}}\right)\geq\sum_{\nu=1}^{k}\ell(d_{i_{\nu}})-(k-1)\geq2k+1>0.
\]
Hence $d_{i}$ are free inside $\mathbb{F}_{2}$, and so are the $v_{i}=d_{1}\cdots d_{i}$.

Consider now the signed sum
\[
\widetilde{R}_{m}=\sum_{j=2}^{m}\lambda(g_{j})-\sum_{j=1}^{m}\lambda(h_{j})=R_{m}-1.
\]
Lemma \ref{lem:sparse-clt} now shows that $(2m-1)^{-1/2}\widetilde{R}_{m}$
(and thus $(2m-1)^{-1/2}R_{m}$) converges in $*$-distribution to
the circular law. Consequently the spectral distributions $\nu_{m}$
of 
\[
A_{m}=\frac{R_{m}R_{m}^{*}}{2m}
\]
converge weakly to the free Poisson law
\[
d\nu(s)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{4-s}{s}}\,\mathbf{1}_{(0,4)}(s)\,ds
\]
(see \cite[Example 15.15 and Proposition 12.13]{NicaSpeicher}). In
particular, $\nu(\{0\})=0$.

Now let 
\[
\widetilde{x}_{m}=R_{m}^{*}(1+R_{m}R_{m}^{*})^{-1}\delta_{e}.
\]
Since 
\[
R_{m}\widetilde{x}_{m}-\delta_{e}=-(1+R_{m}R_{m}^{*})^{-1}\delta_{e},
\]
the spectral theorem gives 
\[
\|\widetilde{x}_{m}\|_{2}^{2}+\|R_{m}\widetilde{x}_{m}-\delta_{e}\|_{2}^{2}=\tau\bigl((1+R_{m}R_{m}^{*})^{-1}\bigr).
\]
Thus, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\begin{aligned}\tau\bigl((1+R_{m}R_{m}^{*})^{-1}\bigr) & =\int\frac{1}{1+2ms}\,d\nu_{m}(s)\\
 & \leq\nu_{m}([0,\varepsilon])+\frac{1}{1+2m\varepsilon}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Since $\nu(\{0\})=0$, we may choose $\varepsilon>0$ such that $\nu([0,\varepsilon])<\eta^{2}/8$.
Weak convergence gives
\[
\limsup_{m\to\infty}\nu_{m}([0,\varepsilon])\leq\nu([0,\varepsilon])<\frac{\eta^{2}}{8}.
\]
We can therefore choose $m$ sufficiently large that both $\nu_{m}([0,\varepsilon])<\eta^{2}/8$
and $(1+2m\varepsilon)^{-1}<\eta^{2}/8$. The preceding identity and
bound then give
\[
\|\widetilde{x}_{m}\|_{2}^{2}+\|R_{m}\widetilde{x}_{m}-\delta_{e}\|_{2}^{2}<\frac{\eta^{2}}{4},
\]
so each of the two norms is less than $\eta/2$.

The vector $\widetilde{x}_{m}$ is real. Approximate $\widetilde{x}_{m}$
by a finitely supported real vector $x$ with 
\[
\|x-\widetilde{x}_{m}\|_{2}<\frac{\eta}{2(1+\|R_{m}\|)}.
\]
Then $\|x\|_{2}<\eta$ and $\|R_{m}x-\delta_{e}\|_{2}<\eta$. Since
$w_{m}$ is a nonempty positive word and $c(w_{m})=R_{m}x$, this
proves the lemma.

label: lem:scalar-conjugate-variable
title: \protect\lemmaname
body_md:
\label{lem:scalar-conjugate-variable}Let $V$ be a Haar unitary.
Identify $C^{*}(V)$ with $C(\mathbb{T})$ by identifying $V$ with
the complex coordinate, and regard tensors in $C^{*}(V)\otimes C^{*}(V)^{\mathrm{op}}$
as functions on $\mathbb{T}^{2}$. Denote by $m$ the Haar measure.

For every $\epsilon_{0}>0$, there is a real-valued antisymmetric
Laurent polynomial $q$ such that the inner derivation $d$ on $\mathop{{*}\text{-}\mathrm{Alg}}\nolimits(V)$
given by $d(g)=gq-qg$ and the selfadjoint element $p\in\mathop{{*}\text{-}\mathrm{Alg}}\nolimits(V)$
given by $p(\zeta)=2\int q(\zeta,\omega)\,dm(\omega)$ satisfy 
\[
p=d^{*}(1\otimes1),\qquad\|d(p)-1\otimes1\|_{\mathrm{rc}}<\epsilon_{0}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Given a continuous real-valued antisymmetric $q\in C(\mathbb{T}^{2})$,
let $T_{q}$ be its integral operator on $L^{2}(\mathbb{T},m)$. Under
the standard identification with Hilbert-{}-Schmidt operators, the
inner derivation $dg=gq-qg$ becomes $[M_{g},T_{q}]$, where $M_{g}$
is multiplication by $g$. Since $T_{q}$ is real and $T_{q}^{*}=-T_{q}$,
the commutator formula of \cite[Proposition 2.6]{ShlyakhtenkoPartialConjugates}
gives 
\[
d^{*}(1\otimes1)=2T_{q}1=2\int q(\,\cdot\,,\omega)\,dm(\omega).
\]

Let $f:\mathbb{T}\to[-2,2]$ be continuous and such that $f_{*}m=\mu$
is the semicircular measure. Write $x=f(\zeta)$, $y=f(\omega)$.
For $t>0$ let 
\[
\begin{aligned}q_{t}(x,y) & =\frac{x-y}{(x-y)^{2}+t^{2}},\\
h_{t}(x) & =x-2\int q_{t}(x,y)\,d\mu(y).
\end{aligned}
\]
The semicircle Cauchy transform \cite[Lemma 2.21]{NicaSpeicher} gives
\[
h_{t}(x)=\operatorname{Re}\sqrt{(x+it)^{2}-4},\qquad\|h_{t}\|_{\infty}\leq\sqrt{2t},
\]
using the branch $\sqrt{z^{2}-4}\sim z$ at infinity. Also, $\int h_{t}\,d\mu=0$
by centering and antisymmetry.

For a kernel $q$ and a real function $r$, write
\[
q[r](x,y)=q(x,y)+\frac{r(x)-r(y)}{2}.
\]
If $\int r\,d\mu=0$, this correction changes $2\int q(x,y)\,d\mu(y)$
by $r(x)$. Take $\widetilde{q}_{t}=q_{t}[h_{t}]$, and let $\widetilde{d}_{t}$
be the derivation associated with the kernel $\widetilde{q}_{t}(f(\zeta),f(\omega))$.
Then $\widetilde{d}_{t}^{*}(1\otimes1)=f$. Moreover, 
\[
\widetilde{d}_{t}f-1\otimes1=-\frac{t^{2}}{(x-y)^{2}+t^{2}}+\frac{(x-y)(h_{t}(x)-h_{t}(y))}{2}.
\]
Since the semicircle density is at most $1/\pi$,
\[
\left\Vert \frac{t^{2}}{(x-y)^{2}+t^{2}}\right\Vert _{rc}^{2}\leq\frac{4}{\pi}\int\frac{t^{4}}{(u^{2}+t^{2})^{2}}du=2t
\]
and
\[
\left\Vert \frac{(x-y)(h_{t}(x)-h_{t}(y))}{2}\right\Vert _{rc}\leq4\Vert x\Vert_{\infty}\left\Vert h_{t}\right\Vert _{\infty}\leq8\sqrt{2t}
\]
so that
\[
\|\widetilde{d}_{t}f-1\otimes1\|_{\mathrm{rc}}\leq9\sqrt{2t}.
\]

Fix $t$ with $9\sqrt{2t}<\epsilon_{0}/2$. Approximate the continuous
kernel $\widetilde{q}_{t}(f(\zeta),f(\omega))$ uniformly by real-valued
antisymmetric Laurent polynomials $q_{n}$. Put 
\[
p_{n}(\zeta)=2\int q_{n}(\zeta,\omega)\,dm(\omega),\qquad d_{n}(g)(\zeta,\omega)=(g(\zeta)-g(\omega))q_{n}(\zeta,\omega).
\]
Then $p_{n}=d_{n}^{*}(1\otimes1)$ and, as $n\to\infty$, 
\[
p_{n}\longrightarrow f,\qquad d_{n}(p_{n})\longrightarrow\widetilde{d}_{t}f
\]
uniformly. Since $\|H\|_{\mathrm{rc}}\leq2\|H\|_{\infty}$, the desired
estimate holds for $p=p_{n}$, $q=q_{n}$ and $d=d_{n}$ when $n$
is sufficiently large.
head: environment

label: prop:lifted-conjugate-variable
title: \protect\propositionname
body_md:
\label{prop:lifted-conjugate-variable}Let $x\in B_{0}$, $w\in G\setminus\{e\}$
and $c:G\to\ell^{2}(G)$ be as in Lemma \ref{lem:cocycle}. Put
\[
\rho=\|x\|_{2},\qquad\theta=\|c(w)-\delta_{e}\|_{2},
\]
and assume that $\theta<1/4$.

For a real-valued antisymmetric Laurent polynomial $\hat{q}(\zeta,\omega)=\sum\hat{q}_{j,k}\zeta^{j}\omega^{k}$,
let $\hat{K}=(\zeta-\omega)\hat{q}(\zeta,\omega)\omega^{-1}$, $Q=\Delta(x)\#\hat{K}(u_{w})$,
and consider the derivation $\delta:B_{0}\to B_{0}\otimes B_{0}^{\mathrm{op}}$
defined by
\[
\delta(u_{a})=Qu_{a}-u_{a}Q,\qquad\delta(u_{b})=0.
\]
Then we can choose $\hat{q}$ so that $\Vert\hat{q}-q\Vert_{W}\leq4A_{q}\theta$,
$Q^{\dagger}=-Q$, $\delta$ is real, $\xi=\delta^{*}(1\otimes1)=p(u_{w})$,
and the estimates
\[
\|Q\|_{\mathrm{rc}}\leq8A_{q}\rho,\qquad\|\delta(u_{a})\|_{\mathrm{rc}}\leq16A_{q}\rho,\qquad\|\delta(\xi)-1\otimes1\|_{\mathrm{rc}}\leq\epsilon_{0}+C_{q}\theta
\]
hold.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For any real antisymmetric polynomial $q'$, put $K_{q'}(\zeta,\omega)=(\zeta-\omega)q'(\zeta,\omega)\omega^{-1}$.
Since $K_{q'}^{\dagger}=-K_{q'}$ and $x$ has real coefficients,
$Q_{q'}=\Delta(x)\#K_{q'}(u_{w})$ satisfies $Q_{q'}^{\dagger}=-Q_{q'}$.
Define $\delta_{q'}$ on $B_{0}$ by $\delta_{q'}(u_{a})=[Q_{q'},u_{a}]$
and $\delta_{q'}(u_{b})=0$. The cocycle identity then gives
\[
\delta_{q'}(u_{g})=(\Delta(c(g))\#K_{q'}(u_{w}))u_{g}\qquad(g\in G).
\]

Set
\[
\gamma_{n}=c(w)(w^{n}),\qquad\sigma_{n}=\frac{\gamma_{n}+\gamma_{-n}}{2},\qquad F(\zeta,\omega)=\sum_{n}\gamma_{n}\zeta^{n}\omega^{-n}.
\]
These coefficients are real and finitely supported. For a Laurent
polynomial $g$ the chain rule and definition of $\delta_{q'}$ give:
\[
(\tau\otimes\tau)(\delta_{q'}(g(u_{w})))=\iint(g(\zeta)-g(\omega))F(\zeta,\omega)q'(\zeta,\omega)\,dm(\zeta)\,dm(\omega).
\]
Since $F(\omega,\zeta)=\overline{F(\zeta,\omega)}$ and $q'$ is antisymmetric,
the real centered Laurent polynomial
\[
\xi_{q'}(\zeta)=2\int q'(\zeta,\omega)\operatorname{Re}F(\zeta,\omega)\,dm(\omega),\qquad\operatorname{Re}F=\sum_{n}\sigma_{n}\zeta^{n}\omega^{-n}
\]
satisfies
\[
(\tau\otimes\tau)(\delta_{q'}z)=\tau(\xi_{q'}(u_{w})z)\qquad\bigl(\forall z\in\mathop{{*}\text{-}\mathrm{Alg}}\nolimits(u_{w})\bigr).
\]

This identity holds on all of $B_{0}$. Indeed, write $K_{q'}(\zeta,\omega)=\sum_{r,s}\kappa_{rs}\zeta^{r}\omega^{s}$.
Each tensor in the expansion of $\delta_{q'}(u_{g})$ has the form
\[
u_{h}u_{w}^{r}\otimes(u_{w}^{s}u_{h}^{*}u_{g})^{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Both factors have nonzero trace only if $h=w^{-r}$ and $g=w^{-(r+s)}$.
Thus, for $g\notin\langle w\rangle$, both sides of the preceding
identity vanish. By linearity the identity holds for every $z\in\mathbb{C}G$,
proving that $1\otimes1\in\operatorname{Dom}(\delta_{q'}^{*})$ and
\[
\delta_{q'}^{*}(1\otimes1)=\xi_{q'}(u_{w})
\]
where the adjoint of $\delta_{q'}$ is computed by regarding $\delta_{q'}$
as an unbounded operator $\delta_{q'}:B_{0}\to L^{2}(L(G)\otimes L(G)^{op})$.

Apply the correction $q[r]$ from Lemma \ref{lem:scalar-conjugate-variable},
now with the weight $\operatorname{Re}F$. For a centered real polynomial
$r(\zeta)=\sum_{n\ne0}r_{n}\zeta^{n}$, the preceding formula gives
\[
\xi_{q[r]}(\zeta)-\xi_{q}(\zeta)=\sum_{n\ne0}(\gamma_{0}-\sigma_{n})r_{n}\zeta^{n}.
\]
The bounds $|\gamma_{0}-1|\leq\theta$ and $|\sigma_{n}|\leq\theta$
for $n\ne0$ imply
\[
\|p-\xi_{q}\|_{\mathrm{W}}\leq2A_{q}\theta,\qquad\gamma_{0}-\sigma_{n}\geq1-2\theta>1/2\quad(n\ne0).
\]
Writing $p-\xi_{q}=\sum_{n\ne0}\beta_{n}\zeta^{n}$, set
\[
r(\zeta)=\sum_{n\ne0}\frac{\beta_{n}}{\gamma_{0}-\sigma_{n}}\zeta^{n},\qquad\hat{q}=q[r].
\]
Then $r$ is real and centered, $\|r\|_{\mathrm{W}}\leq4A_{q}\theta$,
and $\xi_{\hat{q}}=p$. Take $\delta=\delta_{\hat{q}}$.

Since $\theta<1/4$, we have $\|\hat{q}\|_{\mathrm{W}}\leq2A_{q}$
and $\|\hat{K}\|_{\mathrm{W}}\leq4A_{q}$. The coefficient estimate
above and the bimodule inequality therefore give
\[
\|Q\|_{\mathrm{rc}}\leq2\rho\|\hat{K}\|_{\mathrm{W}}\leq8A_{q}\rho,\qquad\|\delta(u_{a})\|_{\mathrm{rc}}\leq2\|Q\|_{\mathrm{rc}}.
\]
Let $\hat{d}(g)=(g(\zeta)-g(\omega))\hat{q}(\zeta,\omega)$ be the
derivation defined on $\mathop{{*}\text{-}\mathrm{Alg}}\nolimits(u_{w})$.
The identity
\[
\delta(u_{w})-\hat{d}(u_{w})=(\Delta(c(w)-\delta_{e})\#\hat{K}(u_{w}))u_{w}
\]
and the Leibniz rule give
\[
\|\delta(p(u_{w}))-\hat{d}(p(u_{w}))\|_{\mathrm{rc}}\leq2\theta\|\hat{K}\|_{\mathrm{W}}L_{p}\leq8A_{q}\theta L_{p}.
\]

Finally,
\[
((\hat{d}-d)p)(\zeta,\omega)=\frac{(p(\zeta)-p(\omega))(r(\zeta)-r(\omega))}{2}.
\]
Using $\|H\|_{\mathrm{rc}}\leq2\|H\|_{\infty}$ and Lemma \ref{lem:scalar-conjugate-variable},
we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}\|\delta(\xi)-1\otimes1\|_{\mathrm{rc}} & \leq\epsilon_{0}+8A_{q}\theta L_{p}+4\|p\|_{\infty}\|r\|_{\mathrm{W}}\\
 & \leq\epsilon_{0}+C_{q}\theta.
\end{aligned}
\]

label: cor:conjugate-variable-data
title: \protect\corollaryname
body_md:
\label{cor:conjugate-variable-data}For every $\eta,\epsilon,\kappa>0$,
there is a real derivation $\delta:\mathbb{C}G\to\mathbb{C}G\otimes(\mathbb{C}G)^{\mathrm{op}}$
such that
\[
\delta(u_{b})=0,\qquad\xi=\delta^{*}(1\otimes1)\in\mathbb{C}G,
\]
\[
\|\delta(u_{a})\|_{\mathrm{rc}}<\eta,\qquad\|\delta(\xi)-1\otimes1\|_{\mathrm{rc}}<\epsilon.
\]
Moreover, $\delta$ is inner on $\mathop{{*}\text{-}\mathrm{Alg}}\nolimits(u_{a})$,
given by $\delta(y)=[Q,y]$, $y\in\mathop{{*}\text{-}\mathrm{Alg}}\nolimits(u_{a})$,
with $Q$ satisfying $Q^{\dagger}=-Q$ and $\|Q\|_{\mathrm{rc}}<\kappa$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First apply Lemma \ref{lem:scalar-conjugate-variable} with $\epsilon_{0}<\epsilon/2$,
fixing $q,p$ and hence $A_{q},C_{q}$. Choose $0<\eta_{0}<1/4$ so
that
\[
16A_{q}\eta_{0}<\eta,\qquad8A_{q}\eta_{0}<\kappa,\qquad C_{q}\eta_{0}<\epsilon/2.
\]
Apply Lemma \ref{lem:cocycle} with tolerance $\eta_{0}$. Then $\rho,\theta<\eta_{0}$,
and Proposition \ref{prop:lifted-conjugate-variable} gives the required
derivation, with $\xi=p(u_{w})$ exactly and with the asserted small
inner implementation. All coefficients and the conjugate variable
lie in the group algebra.

label: thm:free-absorption
title: \protect\theoremname
body_md:
\label{thm:free-absorption}Let $2\leq n<\infty$, let $u_{1},\ldots,u_{n}$
be the canonical free Haar generators of $B_{n}=C_{\mathrm{red}}^{*}(\mathbb{F}_{n})$,
and put $A_{n}=C^{*}(u_{2},\ldots,u_{n})$. If $S$ is standard semicircular
and free from $B_{n}$, then
\[
B_{n}\subset C_{n}=B_{n}*_{\mathrm{red}}C^{*}(S)
\]
has CAAP relative to $A_{n}$, with small unitary implementation on
$C^{*}(u_{1})$.

Equivalently, there are surjective trace-preserving isomorphisms $\Phi_{j}:B_{n}\to C_{n}$
fixing $A_{n}$ pointwise and converging pointwise in norm to inclusion,
with
\[
\Phi_{j}(u_{1})=U_{j}u_{1}U_{j}^{*},\qquad U_{j}\in\mathcal{U}(C_{n}),\qquad\|U_{j}-1\|\longrightarrow0.
\]

In particular,
\[
B_{n}\cong B_{n}*_{\mathrm{red}}C^{*}(S).
\]

Passing to the GNS representation, the inclusion
\[
L(\mathbb{F}_{n})\subset L(\mathbb{F}_{n})*L(\mathbb{Z})\cong L(\mathbb{F}_{n+1})
\]
has AAP relative to $W^{*}(u_{2},\ldots,u_{n})$, with small unitary
implementation on $W^{*}(u_{1})$. In particular, $L(\mathbb{F}_{n})\cong L(\mathbb{F}_{n+1})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $n=2$, apply Corollary \ref{cor:conjugate-variable-data} with
$u_{a}=u_{1}$ and $u_{b}=u_{2}$. Its derivations satisfy the hypotheses
of Proposition \ref{prop:absorption} on $B_{0}=\mathbb{C}\mathbb{F}_{2}$,
with $A=\mathop{{*}\text{-}\mathrm{Alg}}\nolimits(u_{2})$ and $X=u_{1}$,
and the bound for the inner restriction to $\mathop{{*}\text{-}\mathrm{Alg}}\nolimits(u_{1})$.
The proposition gives CAAP relative to $C^{*}(u_{2})$, with small
unitary implementation on $C^{*}(u_{1})$. By Proposition \ref{prop:caap},
we may choose surjective trace-preserving isomorphisms
\[
\Psi_{j}:B_{2}\longrightarrow B_{2}*_{\mathrm{red}}C^{*}(S)
\]
fixing $u_{2}$ and converging pointwise in norm to inclusion, and
such that $\Psi_{j}(u_{1})=U_{j}u_{1}U_{j}^{*}$ and $\|U_{j}-1\|\to0$.

For $n>2$, put $D=C^{*}(u_{3},\ldots,u_{n})$, so $B_{n}=B_{2}*_{\mathrm{red}}D$.
We therefore obtain surjective trace-preserving isomorphisms
\[
\begin{aligned}\Phi_{j}=\Psi_{j}*\mathrm{id}_{D}:\ B_{n} & \longrightarrow(B_{2}*_{\mathrm{red}}C^{*}(S))*_{\mathrm{red}}D\\
 & \cong(B_{2}*_{\mathrm{red}}D)*_{\mathrm{red}}C^{*}(S)=C_{n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The maps $\Phi_{j}$ fix $u_{2}$ and $D$, hence fix $A_{n}$, and
retain $\Phi_{j}(u_{1})=U_{j}u_{1}U_{j}^{*}$ with the same unitaries,
and converge pointwise to the inclusion $B_{n}\subset C_{n}$. The
rest of the statements are straightforward. For the von Neumann algebra
application, it only remains to pass to the von Neumann algebras,
noting that $W^{*}(S)\cong L(\mathbb{Z})$ since the semicircular
measure is diffuse.
head: environment

label: cor:countable-absorption
title: \protect\corollaryname
body_md:
\label{cor:countable-absorption}Let $B_{n},A_{n}$ be as in Theorem
\ref{thm:free-absorption}, and let $(S_{j})_{j\in J}$ be a nonempty
finite or countable free standard semicircular family, free from $B_{n}$.
The inclusion
\[
B_{n}\subset C^{*}(B_{n},S_{j}:j\in J)
\]
has CAAP relative to $A_{n}$, with small unitary implementation on
$C^{*}(u_{1})$. Consequently,
\[
B_{n}\cong B_{n}*_{\mathrm{red}}C^{*}(S_{j}:j\in J).
\]
The generated von Neumann inclusion has AAP relative to $W^{*}(A_{n})$,
with small unitary implementation on $W^{*}(u_{1})$. If $J$ is infinite,
this gives $L(\mathbb{F}_{n})\cong L(\mathbb{F}_{\infty})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Enumerate the family and put $D_{0}=B_{n}$, $D_{k}=C^{*}(B_{n},S_{1},\ldots,S_{k})$,
and $E=C^{*}(u_{1})$. Theorem \ref{thm:free-absorption} gives relative
CAAP for $D_{0}\subset D_{1}$ with small unitary implementation on
$E$. Inductively, suppose that $B_{n}\subset D_{k}$ has this strengthened
property. Choose a surjective trace-preserving isomorphism $\Theta:B_{n}\to D_{k}$
fixing $A_{n}$ and satisfying $\Theta|_{E}=\operatorname{Ad}T|_{E}$
for a unitary $T\in D_{k}$. The isomorphism $\Theta*\mathrm{id}_{C^{*}(S_{k+1})}$
carries the inclusion $B_{n}\subset B_{n}*_{\mathrm{red}}C^{*}(S_{k+1})$
to $D_{k}\subset D_{k+1}$. Thus the latter has relative CAAP with
small unitary implementation on $\Theta(E)=TET^{*}$. Remark \ref{rem:implementation}
gives the same property on $E$, and Proposition \ref{prop:permanence}(1)
gives it for $B_{n}\subset D_{k+1}$. This proves the assertion for
finite families.

For an infinite family, put $D_{\infty}=\overline{\bigcup_{k}D_{k}}^{\|\cdot\|}$.
Proposition \ref{prop:permanence}(2) gives CAAP for $B_{n}\subset D_{\infty}$
relative to $A_{n}$, with small unitary implementation on $E$. Proposition
\ref{prop:caap} gives the stated $C^{*}$-isomorphism.
head: environment

label: lem:small-conjugation
title: \protect\lemmaname
body_md:
\label{lem:small-conjugation}Let $u,v$ be free Haar unitaries, and
let $(S_{j})_{j\in J}$ be a nonempty finite or countable free standard
semicircular family, free from them. Put $R=C^{*}(u,v,S_{j}:j\in J)$.
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a unitary $U\in R$ such that
\[
\|U-1\|<\varepsilon,\qquad R=C^{*}(UuU^{*},v),
\]
and $UuU^{*},v$ are free Haar unitaries.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Corollary \ref{cor:countable-absorption} with $n=2$, $u_{1}=u$
and $u_{2}=v$. By the strengthened form of Proposition \ref{prop:caap},
there are a surjective trace-preserving isomorphism $\Phi:C^{*}(u,v)\to R$
fixing $v$ and a unitary $U\in R$ such that
\[
\Phi(u)=UuU^{*},\qquad\|U-1\|<\varepsilon.
\]
Surjectivity gives $R=C^{*}(UuU^{*},v)$, and trace preservation gives
the free Haar law of $UuU^{*},v$.

label: thm:freeProductsAbsorb
title: \protect\theoremname
body_md:
\label{thm:freeProductsAbsorb}Let $(A_{i},\tau_{i})$, $i=1,2$ be
separable $C^{*}$-algebras with faithful tracial states, and suppose
that there exist Haar unitaries $u\in A_{1}$ and $v\in A_{2}$. Let
$J$ be a finite or countable set, and let $S_{j}:j\in J$ be a free
semicircular family free from $A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}$.

Then for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists a unitary $U\in C^{*}(u,v,S_{j}:j\in J)$,
$\Vert U-1\Vert<\epsilon$, and so that $C^{*}(A_{1},A_{2},S_{j}:j\in J)=C^{*}(UA_{1}U^{*},A_{2})$
and moreover $UA_{1}U^{*}$ and $A_{2}$ are freely independent. Thus
$A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}\subset A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}*_{\textrm{red}}C^{*}(S_{j}:j\in J)$
has CAAP.

In particular, $A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}\cong A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}*_{\textrm{red}}C^{*}(S_{j}:j\in J)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Clearly, we can assume that $J$ is nonempty. Let $Q=C^{*}(S_{j}:j\in J)$.
For every $\epsilon>0$, Lemma \ref{lem:small-conjugation} yields
a unitary $U\in C^{*}(u,v,S_{j}:j\in J)$ so that $\Vert U-1\Vert<\epsilon$,
and so that the map $\Phi:u\mapsto UuU^{*},\ v\mapsto v$ extends
to a $*$-isomorphism of $B=C^{*}(u,v)$ with $C^{*}(u,v,S_{j}:j\in J)=B*_{\textrm{red}}Q$,
and so that $UuU^{*}$ and $v$ are freely independent.

Let $\mathcal{A}_{j}=W^{*}(A_{j})$, $\mathcal{Q}=W^{*}(S_{j}:j\in J)$
in the GNS representation corresponding to tracial states. We repeatedly
use the identity $M*_{B}(B*N)=M*N$ valid for amalgamated free products
of von Neumann algebras taken with respect to trace-preserving conditional
expectations.

Let now $\mathcal{A}=\mathcal{A}_{1}*\mathcal{A}_{2}$. Then
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{A}*\mathcal{Q} & =\mathcal{A}_{1}*\mathcal{Q}*\mathcal{A}_{2}=W^{*}(\mathcal{A}_{1},u,v,Q)*_{W^{*}(v)}\mathcal{A}_{2}\\
 & =(\mathcal{A}_{1}*_{W^{*}(u)}W^{*}(u,v,Q))*_{W^{*}(v)}\mathcal{A}_{2}\\
 & =(U\mathcal{A}_{1}U^{*}*_{W^{*}(UuU^{*})}W^{*}(u,v,Q))*_{W^{*}(v)}\mathcal{A}_{2}
\end{align*}
because $U\in W^{*}(u,v,Q)$. Since $C^{*}(UuU^{*},v)=C^{*}(u,v,Q)$
also $W^{*}(UuU^{*},v)=W^{*}(u,v,Q)$; moreover $UuU^{*}$ and $v$
are free, so $W^{*}(u,v,Q)=W^{*}(UuU^{*})*W^{*}(v)$. Thus
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{A}*\mathcal{Q} & =(U\mathcal{A}_{1}U^{*}*_{W^{*}(UuU^{*})}W^{*}(u,v,Q))*_{W^{*}(v)}\mathcal{A}_{2}\\
 & =(U\mathcal{A}_{1}U^{*}*_{W^{*}(UuU^{*})}[W^{*}(UuU^{*})*W^{*}(v)])*_{W^{*}(v)}\mathcal{A}_{2}\\
 & =(U\mathcal{A}_{1}U^{*}*W^{*}(v))*_{W^{*}(v)}\mathcal{A}_{2}=W^{*}(U\mathcal{A}_{1}U^{*})*\mathcal{A}_{2}.
\end{align*}

It follows that $U\mathcal{A}_{1}U^{*}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{2}$ are
free in $\mathcal{A}*\mathcal{Q}$. But then $UA_{1}U^{*}$ and $A_{2}$
are free in $A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}*_{\textrm{red}}Q$. It follows
that the maps
\begin{align*}
x & \mapsto UxU^{*},\qquad x\in A_{1},\\
y & \mapsto y,\qquad y\in A_{2}
\end{align*}
extend to a trace-preserving $C^{*}$-monomorphism $\Psi_{\epsilon}$
of $A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}$ into $A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}*_{\textrm{red}}Q$.
Since $\{u,v\}\cup Q\subset C^{*}(UuU^{*},v)$, it follows that the
image of this monomorphism contains both $Q$ and $U$, and thus $A_{1}$
and $A_{2}$, and so is surjective; thus it gives an isomorphism of
$A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}*_{\textrm{red}}Q$ with $A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}$.

Taking $\epsilon\to0$, we see that $\Psi_{\epsilon}$ converges to
the inclusion $A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}\subset A_{1}*_{\textrm{red}}A_{2}*_{\textrm{red}}Q$.

title: \protect\corollaryname
body_md:
Let $J\subset\mathbb{N}$ be a finite or countable set with $|J|\geq2$,
and let $S_{j}:j\in J$ be a free semicircular system. Then 
\[
C^{*}(S_{j}:j\in J)\cong C^{*}(S_{1},S_{2}).
\]
In particular, the isomorphism class of $Q=C^{*}(S_{j}:j\in J)$ does
not depend on the cardinality of $J$.

title: \protect\corollaryname
body_md:
Let $G$ and $H$ be two infinite discrete groups, $J$ be a finite
or countable set, and $S_{j}:j\in J$ a free semicircular family.
Let $Q=C^{*}(S_{j}:j\in J)$. Then 
\[
C_{\mathrm{red}}^{*}(G*H)*_{\mathrm{red}}Q\cong C_{\mathrm{red}}^{*}(G*H).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $G$ is an infinite discrete group, then $C_{\textrm{red}}^{*}(G)$
contains a Haar unitary \cite[Proposition 8.1]{ThielHaarUnitaries}.
head: environment

title: \protect\remarkname
body_md:
More general free products can sometimes be regrouped into free products
that contain Haar unitaries. For example, if four algebras $A_{1},\dots,A_{4}$
contain centered unitaries $z_{i}\in A_{i}$, then $z_{1}z_{2}$ and
$z_{3}z_{4}$ are free Haar unitaries. Thus in particular 
\[
\left(*_{\mathrm{red},\,i=1}^{4}(M_{n_{i}}(\mathbb{C}),\operatorname{tr}_{n_{i}})\right)*_{\mathrm{red}}Q\cong*_{\mathrm{red},\,i=1}^{4}(M_{n_{i}}(\mathbb{C}),\operatorname{tr}_{n_{i}}),\qquad n_{i}\geq2,
\]
where $Q$ as before is generated by a finite or countable free semicircular
family.

label: rem:hirshberg-phillips-1
title: \protect\remarkname
body_md:
\label{rem:hirshberg-phillips-1}Let $I=(C([0,1]),\lambda)$, with
Lebesgue measure, and let $D$ be the countably infinite reduced free
product of $I$ with itself. Then $D\cong Q=C^{*}(S_{1},S_{2},\dots)$,
where $S_{1},S_{2},\dots$ are free semicircular variables.

Let $\mathcal{Z}$ be the Jiang--Su algebra. By a result of Hirshberg--Phillips
\cite[Theorem 3.1]{HirshbergPhillips},
\[
D*_{\textrm{red}}\mathcal{Z}\cong D
\]
(trace-preserving isomorphism). Since $\mathcal{Z}$ contains a Haar
unitary, we can apply Theorem \ref{thm:freeProductsAbsorb} to conclude
that
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{Z}*_{\textrm{red}}\mathcal{Z} & \cong\mathcal{Z}*_{\textrm{red}}\mathcal{Z}*_{\textrm{red}}D\\
 & \cong\mathcal{Z}*_{\textrm{red}}D*_{\textrm{red}}\mathcal{Z}*_{\textrm{red}}D\\
 & \cong D*_{\textrm{red}}D\cong D.
\end{align*}
This answers \cite[Question 4.5]{HirshbergPhillips}.

In particular, reduced free products of $n\geq2$ (or countably infinitely
many) copies of $\mathcal{Z}$ are isomorphic to $\mathcal{Z}*_{\textrm{red}}\mathcal{Z}\cong I*_{\textrm{red}}I$.
head: environment

label: rem:nccw-absorption
title: \protect\remarkname
body_md:
\label{rem:nccw-absorption}More generally, let $E$ be a unital countable
inductive limit of one-dimensional noncommutative CW complexes, equipped
with a faithful tracial state, and suppose that $K_{0}(E)=\mathbb{Z}[1_{E}]$
and $K_{1}(E)=0$. By \cite[Theorem 3.1]{HirshbergPhillips}, $D*_{\mathrm{red}}E\cong D$.
Combining this with Theorem \ref{thm:freeProductsAbsorb}, every $B=A_{1}*_{\mathrm{red}}A_{2}$
as in that theorem satisfies 
\[
B*_{\mathrm{red}}E\cong B.
\]
Examples of $E$ include $C(T)$ for a finite tree $T$, prime dimension-drop
algebras $Z_{p,q}$ with relatively prime $p,q$, and the Jiang--Su
algebra, with any faithful tracial state. In particular, 
\[
C_{\mathrm{red}}^{*}(\mathbb{F}_{m})*_{\mathrm{red}}E\cong C_{\mathrm{red}}^{*}(\mathbb{F}_{m})\qquad(m\in\{2,3,\ldots,\infty\}).
\]

label: prop:elementary
title: \protect\propositionname
body_md:
\label{prop:elementary}If $N\subset M$ has AAP, then the inclusion
is elementary: $N\preceq M$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition \ref{prop:aap}, there are surjective trace-preserving
isomorphisms $\Phi_{j}:N\to M$ converging pointwise in $L^{2}$ to
inclusion. Fix a formula $\varphi$ and a tuple $a=(a_{1},\ldots,a_{k})$
from $N$. Isomorphisms preserve formula values: they preserve the
algebraic operations and trace, and surjectivity identifies the domains
of every infimum and supremum. Hence 
\[
\varphi^{N}(a)=\varphi^{M}(\Phi_{j}(a)).
\]
Since $\|\Phi_{j}(a_{i})\|=\|a_{i}\|$ and $\|\Phi_{j}(a_{i})-a_{i}\|_{2}\to0$,
uniform continuity gives 
\[
\varphi^{N}(a)=\lim_{j\to\infty}\varphi^{M}(\Phi_{j}(a))=\varphi^{M}(a).
\]
head: environment

label: rem:caap-elementary
title: \protect\remarkname
body_md:
\label{rem:caap-elementary}The same proof shows that CAAP implies
elementarity in the language of unital $C^{*}$-algebras, using the
norm metric and norm predicates. For trace-preserving CAAP, one may
also name the trace.

label: prop:classical-aap
title: \protect\propositionname
body_md: \label{prop:classical-aap}The inclusion $N\subset M$ has AAP.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Take $m=2^{n}$ and write $\beta_{m}=\alpha_{\pi/2}^{(m)}$. Since
$N=L^{\infty}(\sigma(J_{m},\xi_{m}))$, 
\[
\beta_{m}(N)=L^{\infty}(\sigma(J_{m},s)).
\]
For $f\in N$, let $f_{m}=\mathbb{E}[f\mid J_{m}]$. The automorphism
$\beta_{m}$ fixes $f_{m}$, so
\[
\|\beta_{m}(f)-f\|_{2}\leq2\|f-f_{m}\|_{2}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Here we use that the dyadic partitions generate $\sigma(x)$ modulo
null sets.

For $z\in M$, the bounded functions
\[
z_{m}=\mathbb{E}[z\mid J_{m},s]\in\beta_{m}(N)
\]
satisfy $\|z-z_{m}\|_{2}\to0$, because the increasing sigma-algebras
$\sigma(J_{2^{n}},s)$ generate $\sigma(x,s)$. Taking $y_{m}=\beta_{m}^{-1}(z_{m})\in N$
verifies condition (1) of Proposition \ref{prop:aap}.
